title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Vulnerability Allows Remote Code Execution
summary: Apache released a security patch for CVE-2026-119618, a critical race condition in mod_http2 that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled.

title: N-able "4EverAble2Shell" Zero-Day Actively Exploited Hours After PoC Release
summary: The N-able N-central platform has a zero-day vulnerability called "4EverAble2Shell" that was actively exploited within hours of proof-of-concept release. Attackers compromised at least 21 systems and deployed cryptocurrency miners; N-able disabled cloud services in response.
takeaways: Zero-day called "4EverAble2Shell"
Actively exploited within hours of PoC release
At least 21 systems compromised
Cryptocurrency miners deployed on servers

title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
summary: Unauthenticated attackers can write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on Cisco Secure Email Gateway systems.
takeaways: CVE-2026-76519 allows unauthenticated remote command execution as root (CVSS 9.8)
Requires File Reputation service enabled and Content Scanner Tools version earlier than 25.3.0.5525
Fixed in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014, 16.5.0-780, and Content Scanner Tools 25.3.0.5525 or later
Active exploitation discovered October 2026; AsyncOS 16.0 requires migration to fixed release
CVE-2026-76519 rated CVSS 9.8; zero-day actively exploited in the wild
Flaw in Advanced Malware Protection; unauthenticated attacker executes root commands via malicious email attachment
Affects SEG physical/virtual appliances and Panorama where File Reputation service enabled
CISA added to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities; federal agencies have Saturday remediation deadline
updatesTitle: Cisco warns of active attacks exploiting critical Secure Email Gateway vulnerability

title: Next.js releases critical security patches for RCE flaws in caching and SVG processing
summary: Next.js released critical security updates on October 14 fixing two remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVSS 9.5 each) and one high-severity denial-of-service flaw. The RCE flaws affect caching in React Server Components and SVG rendering via the sharp library, with fixes available in versions 16
takeaways: Two critical RCE vulnerabilities (CVSS 9.5 each) and one high-severity DoS flaw patched
First RCE affects versions 16.0.0–16.4.0 using cache function; fixed in 16.4.1
Second RCE (CVE-2026-96889) in librsvg/sharp affecting versions 10.0.0–15.5.27 and 16.0.0–16.4.0
DoS flaw affects App Router apps with Server Actions
Patches available in Next.js 16.4.1 (Active LTS) and 15.5.28 (Maintenance LTS)

summary: Google Cloud identified three CPU side-channel vulnerabilities in AMD Turin processors (fifth-generation AMD EPYC) that could allow attackers with code execution on the same processor core to infer sensitive data from other processes or the kernel within virtual machines. title: Google session hijacking campaign exploits calendar invites and live proxies to steal corporate credentials
summary: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing campaign tracked as Operation CloudFire has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. The attack uses Google Calendar invites as the initial lure, with messages arriving via BCC or from organizations the recipient has previously corresponded with. Pre

title: PTC patches critical Windchill and FlexPLM vulnerability enabling remote code execution
summary: PTC released security patches for a critical CVSS 9.2 flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM software that allows unauthenticated remote code execution.

title: Critical Red Hat Quay container registry vulnerability exposed
summary: A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay enables attackers with registry access to read and overwrite all private container images without authentication when anonymous access is enabled.

title: Node.js patches 16 vulnerabilities including critical HTTP/2 crash and data leak flaws
summary: Node.js released fixes for 16 security flaws, including HTTP/2 bugs that allow unauthenticated clients to crash servers and leak sensitive data from other connections.

title: Widespread Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot Globally
summary: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage on November 12 disrupted Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot, OneDrive, and the Admin Center globally. Exchange Online email access failed, Teams calendar and meeting features degraded, and the Service Health portal experienced intermittent loading failures.
takeaways: Tracking codes EX1550543 (Exchange) and TM1550488 (Teams)
Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot, OneDrive affected
Admin Center unavailable for diagnostics
Third-party partners including GoDaddy acknowledged outage

title: SignDrop zero-day exploits Windows CLFS driver to escalate to SYSTEM privileges
summary: A Windows Common Log File System driver zero-day named SignDrop allows local privilege escalation to SYSTEM level. The exploit targets the CLFS authentication mechanism added in October 2025 updates by abusing how .cnpf recovery files are created with privileged process security context.
takeaways: Affects Windows 11 25H2, 26H1, Windows Server 2025
Exploits CLFS authentication via symbolic link redirection
Default configuration on systems older than 90 days is vulnerable
Microsoft has not assigned CVE or released patch as of Nov 12

title: Microsoft Researchers Demonstrate AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated that AI agents can be backdoored by editing fewer than 10 neurons in open-weight models without retraining. The technique, called Lazarus, enables malicious command execution when triggered by specific strings.
takeaways: Nemotron-Terminal-8B: 7 neurons edited (98.8% success rate with 23 training sessions)
Qwen3.6-27B: 6 neurons edited (51-99.5% success rates)
Gemma-4-31B-IT: 99.5% success rates
Requires access to model checkpoint file before deployment; no threat actors observed using technique
Nemotron-Terminal-8B: 7 neurons edited, 98.8% success rate, 23 training sessions
Technique works on Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT models
No retraining required; allows attacker-controlled command execution with agent permissions
No threat actors observed using technique in the wild

title: Over 35,000 Grok-built apps exposed online with leaked credentials
summary: Security researchers found 35,578 of 37,571 Grok-built applications publicly accessible without authentication, with 24 apps created by X and SpaceX staff leaking confidential data including sales proposals, employee lists, and passwords. Exposed organizations included six Fortune 500 companies and
takeaways: 35,578 of 37,571 Grok apps publicly accessible without authentication (94.7%)
24 apps by X/SpaceX staff leaked onboarding plans, sales maps, confidential proposals, employee data
Internal data exposed from 30 organizations across construction, energy, healthcare, defense sectors
~2% of open apps contained high or critical severity material

title: Iran-backed network directed attacks on Jewish and American sites across Europe and US
summary: US prosecutors unsealed an indictment on November 11, 2026, accusing three men of orchestrating attacks on Jewish and American sites across Europe on behalf of Iran's IRGC. The campaign included arson, stabbings, and a plot targeting RAF Fairford, with live-streamed attacks coordinated via FaceTime.
takeaways: Three defendants: Mohammad al-Saadi (Kataib Hezbollah), Mohsen Mohajeri (IRGC), Mohammed Ali al-Hassani (Iraqi national)
Targets: synagogues in Belgium/Netherlands/London, U.S. bank buildings in Amsterdam/Paris, RAF Fairford
~18 attacks/attempted attacks between March–April 2026
Attacks live-streamed over FaceTime with militia logos; IRGC operatives filmed proceedings
Campaign began days after U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran

title: Critical Zoom Workplace vulnerability allows unauthenticated privilege escalation
summary: Zoom released patches for two critical Workplace for Windows vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS 9.6) enabling unauthenticated remote privilege escalation, and CVE-2026-108187 (CVSS 8.1) enabling unauthenticated privilege escalation via network access. No in-the-wild exploitation reported.
takeaways: CVE-2026-108186: CVSS 9.6, affects versions 7.1.0–7.1.7, fixed in 7.1.8
CVE-2026-108187: CVSS 8.1, affects versions before 7.1.5
Both allow unauthenticated remote privilege escalation
No in-the-wild exploitation reported

title: Critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra exploited in active attacks
summary: A critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited to gain administrator access and compromise XCP-ng nodes. The flaw improperly converts authentication tokens to empty objects, allowing attackers to reuse valid tokens and achieve root-level XCP-ng takeover.
takeaways: Affects Xen Orchestra versions before 6.9.2 (stable) and 6.10.1 (latest)
Authentication token converted to empty object {}, returns first token in collection
Exploitation enables arbitrary code execution and full XCP-ng node takeover as root
Threat actor confirmed exploiting alongside zero-day requiring admin privileges
Unauthorized access not logged; no CVE assigned

title: Palo Alto Networks patches critical PAN-OS RCE vulnerability under active exploitation
summary: Palo Alto Networks released security updates for CVE-2026-0322, a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability in PAN-OS management interface currently under active exploitation.
takeaways: CVE-2026-0322 CVSS 8.6; authenticated RCE in PAN-OS management interface
Affects PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls and Panorama; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access not affected
Very limited active exploitation; 3 U.S. IP addresses linked to attempts
CISA deadline: October 17, 2026 for Federal agencies to patch

title: NGINX releases patches for five vulnerabilities including critical RCE and TLS bug
summary: NGINX released patches on October 14 in versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 addressing five vulnerabilities, including three critical memory bugs rated 9.2 on CVSS v4.0 that could crash worker processes or enable remote code execution, plus a TLS client-certificate verification flaw rated 8.3.
takeaways: Three critical memory bugs rated 9.2 on CVSS v4.0 could crash workers or enable RCE
TLS vulnerability (8.3 CVSS) present since version 1.23.2 (October 2022) affects shared session caches
Fifth HTTP/3 flaw (6.9 CVSS) allows clients to inject extra bytes into backend requests
All vulnerabilities require specific configuration directives to expose
No active attacks reported as of October 15; none in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog

title: Hackers deploy PEERSTITCH malware on FortiGate firewalls via Fortinet vulnerabilities
summary: Attackers exploited Fortinet vulnerabilities to install PEERSTITCH, a stealthy ARM64 malware on FortiGate firewalls in a telecom organization breach. The memory-resident malware leaves no disk artifacts, opens no ports, and communicates through legitimate process traffic, enabling long-term access t
takeaways: CVE-2024-47575 exploited against centralized FortiManager appliance for initial compromise
CVE-2025-61624 exploited via FortiOS auto-script path traversal to deploy PEERSTITCH malware
PEERSTITCH is memory-resident ARM64 malware leaving no persistent binary on disk
Attackers exfiltrated configurations and cryptographic material for 500+ managed firewalls
Intrusion tracked as cluster CL-STA-0954 (aka UNC5820)

title: Drupal patches critical Field UI vulnerability allowing unauthenticated RCE
summary: Drupal released critical security patches on October 14 fixing a Field UI vulnerability (CVE-2026-108097) rated 19 out of 25 on Drupal's risk scale that enables unauthenticated remote code execution through contributed modules. Unpatched Drupal versions 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below, and versio
takeaways: CVE-2026-108097 rated 19/25 on Drupal risk scale enabling unauthenticated RCE

28.5% of reporting sites (151,442 of 531,499) on affected branches receiving no fix
Field UI pre-render step runs arbitrary PHP callables without validation

title: International operation dismantles Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware infrastructure
summary: An international law enforcement operation dismantled infrastructure supporting three major malware tools: Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC. Police seized approximately 6.4 million stolen logins from over 40,000 victims and took down 235 servers and 257 domains.
takeaways: Gootloader infected at least 25,000 computers since 2018
Gootloader used against 44 U.S. ransomware victims, causing ~$28.8M losses
German police: Gootloader infected millions since first appearing in 2020
Police removed 14 Gootloader servers, 218 domains, and malware from 681 hacked websites
CastleRAT: 120 servers, 39 domains seized
6.4 million stolen logins from 40,000+ victims recovered
Total takedown: 235 servers, 257 domains

title: SilentAir spying group hijacks Asian telecom networks to intercept SMS 2FA and spy on Taiwan
summary: SilentAir, a newly identified espionage group, hijacked telecom operator equipment across six Asian countries to intercept SMS messages and calls of selected targets, primarily in Taiwan. The group diverted communications using fraudulent UpdateLocation messages, with interception accounting for 18.
takeaways: Infrastructure identified in at least 6 Asian countries
Primarily targeted Taiwan political and government VIPs
Used fraudulent UpdateLocation messages via SS7 and Diameter protocols
Intercepted 2FA codes during call/text diversion
18.3% interception rate vs. 2.1% for commercial operators
Activity tracked from early 2025 onward in campaign bursts
Enea assessed as state-level actor with high confidence

title: Check Point releases emergency patches for actively exploited zero-day vulnerability
summary: Check Point Software released emergency patches for CVE-2026-50751, a critical zero-day vulnerability in its VPN and firewall products. The flaw exploits a logic error in certificate validation, allowing unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication on IKEv1 deployments; exploitation began in M
takeaways: CVE-2026-50751: CVSS 9.3 severity
Affects Mobile Access, SSL VPN, Remote Access VPN, Spark Firewalls
Logic error in certificate validation enables unauthenticated VPN connections
Exploitation began May 7, 2026; accelerated early June
Qilin ransomware affiliate involved in at least one attack
Only IKEv1 deployments vulnerable
CVE-2026-50752 (CVSS 7.4) also identified; no known exploitation reported

title: TSMC Employee Data Exposed via Third-Party Cloud Provider Breach
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company confirmed that approximately 46,000 employee records totaling 6.9 GB were exposed through a third-party cloud service provider. Hackers posted the data for sale on underground forums, initially asking for 3 Bitcoin (~$220,000).
takeaways: ~46,000 current and former employee records exposed
6.9 GB of data including names, DOB, job titles, ID numbers, bank account info
Exposed on DarkForums and BreachForums
Initial asking price: 3 Bitcoin (~$220,000/NT$7.4M)
One-week deadline before threatening full public release
TSMC: no evidence of internal system breach
Production and customer data unaffected

title: SCKit Worm-Like Malware Targets Managed Service Providers in ScreenConnect Attacks
summary: A new worm-like malware toolkit called SCKit has been deployed in ScreenConnect attacks to spread from customer devices to MSP technician systems and compromise additional networks.

title: Threat Actors Compromise 4,837 GitHub Accounts to Steal Cloud Credentials in 'wfx-loot' Campaign
summary: A campaign called 'wfx-loot' exploited 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to probe repositories, open malicious pull requests, and push secrets-stealing malware.
updatesTitle: Attacker uses 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts to deploy CI secret stealer across 1,800+ repositories

title: Attackers Exploit AWS Credentials to Compromise Cloud Environments
summary: Hackers are leveraging compromised AWS access keys to breach multiple organizations' cloud infrastructure.

title: Microsoft patches 1,259 vulnerabilities including exploited Outlook flaw; patch volume exceeds 1,000 for second consecutive month
summary: Microsoft released 1,259 security patches on November 11, the second consecutive month exceeding 1,000 vulnerabilities. Updates include 63 critical flaws and address an actively exploited zero-day in Microsoft Outlook that leaks NTLMv2 hashes without user warning.
takeaways: 1,259 total vulnerabilities: 726 Windows, 174 Office, 61 Developer Tools, 59 SQL Server, 27 SharePoint
Moderate-severity Outlook zero-day (CVE-2026-124194, CVSS 6.5) actively exploited
Over 5,100 CVEs addressed in 2026 to date
CISA deadline for federal agencies: Nov 24, 2026

title: N-able patches zero-day vulnerabilities in N-central RMM platform
summary: N-able responded to public disclosure of critical zero-day vulnerabilities in its N-central RMM platform by taking hosted environments offline. A GitHub account published 33 alleged vulnerabilities including unauthenticated XXE injection chainable to RCE.
takeaways: 33 alleged vulnerabilities disclosed under title 'Able2Shell' on GitHub
Unauthenticated XXE injection can chain into remote code execution
N-central manages systems, deploys software, and maintains privileged access to endpoints
No active exploitation observed at time of advisory

title: eMudhra revokes 8 additional CAs following earlier key compromise
summary: Certificate authority eMudhra revoked 8 more intermediate certificate authorities as fallout from its October key compromise incident, despite these CAs not having weakened keys.

title: Siemens and Industrial Control Systems Face High-Severity Vulnerabilities Ahead of Patch Tuesday
summary: Multiple critical flaws in industrial equipment from Siemens, Phoenix Contact, Johnson Controls, and Hitachi Energy require immediate patching.

title: Intel and AMD Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities in Chipmaker Patch Tuesday
summary: Intel and AMD disclosed more than 200 security vulnerabilities, including critical flaws in Intel TDX and multiple AMD graphics bugs.

title: UK Legal Aid Agency breach exposed records dating to 1978
summary: A cyberattack on Britain's Legal Aid Agency exposed records dating back decades, far more extensive than initially revealed.
takeaways: Hack occurred April 2025; data exfiltrated includes records dating to 1978
Earlier disclosure: 2007+; October 14 revelation: vast majority from 1990s–2000s; small number pre-2007
No complete record of single legal aid case affected; limited probation data also accessed

title: Langflow critical RCE flaw exploited in 1,423 honeypot attacks
summary: A critical authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Langflow (CVE-2026-105740, CVSS 9.9) affecting versions prior to 1.9.0 has been exploited in 1,423 honeypot attacks since September 19, 2026. Non-admin authenticated users can inject malicious MCP servers to execute arbitrary OS command
takeaways: CVE-2026-105740 CVSS 9.9; authenticated RCE in Langflow <1.9.0
1,423 honeypot attacks since September 19; 333 on October 11; 66 on October 15

title: International CSAM Crackdown Nets 95 Arrests Across 17 Countries
summary: Law enforcement from 17 countries arrested 95 suspects in an INTERPOL-coordinated operation targeting child sexual abuse material distribution.

title: SilentAir attackers intercept calls and SMS from within mobile networks
summary: Security researchers warn that SilentAir hackers infiltrated mobile network infrastructure to intercept calls and text messages, primarily targeting Taiwanese subscribers.

title: AI agent prompt injection vulnerability could enable unauthorized data export
summary: Security research demonstrates how AI agents can be compromised through embedded instructions in tickets to perform unintended actions like exporting records.

title: Citrix releases patches for 10 critical NetScaler vulnerabilities
summary: Citrix has released patches addressing 10 critical vulnerabilities in NetScaler that could lead to denial-of-service or unexpected behavior.

title: Hirudo Android RAT replaces banking apps with trojanized versions
summary: Hirudo is a novel Android remote access trojan combining banking malware and full RAT capabilities, delivered via droppers embedded in seemingly legitimate shopping, adult video, and short drama apps. takeaways: Hirudo targets 8 Indonesian banking apps; code hints at China, India, Mexico, Morocco, Thailand expansion

Trojanized replacement apps include hooking engine bypassing signature and Accessibility Services verification
